The record

Written once.
Verifiable forever.

Every certificate we issue is recorded to a public blockchain the moment our desk signs it off. The entry is timestamped and permanent — we cannot edit it, backdate it or quietly withdraw it, and neither can anyone else. Look up a certification number in twenty years and you will get the same answer you get today.

01

Tamper-evident

The certificate is hashed and that fingerprint is written to the chain. Change a word, a photograph or a date afterwards and the fingerprint no longer matches. Verification fails immediately.

02

Independent of us

The entry does not live on our servers. If this company changed hands or closed tomorrow, your certificate would still verify. That is the difference between a ledger and a database.

03

Lifelong, at no further cost

Anchoring is included in every fee, at every tier. No account, no wallet, no renewal and no expiry. Anyone holding the number can check it, for as long as the item exists.

What the ledger does, and what it does not. It guarantees that a certificate is the one we issued and that nothing in it has changed since. It does not, by itself, make a signature authentic — that is a judgement made by an authenticator with the item in hand. The chain secures our opinion. It does not replace it.

The VeriChain authentication desk

01  —  Received

Logged the hour it lands.

Photographed, weighed and given a reference before a single opinion is formed about it. Nothing is charged while it sits in the queue.

02  —  Examined

Then it goes under the loupe.

Ink, paper, pressure, provenance, wear. Two examiners work the item independently, and they have to agree with one another before it moves any further.

03  —  Certified

The signature is the last thing added.

Your Letter is issued the moment the desk approves — digitally, so the proof exists while the item itself is still travelling home to you.

04  —  Anchored

And then it stops being ours to edit.

The certificate is fingerprinted onto a public ledger. No renewal and no expiry: the number issued today still answers in twenty years.

01

Harder to forge

03

A paper letter can be lost, damaged or left behind in a house move. The ledger record cannot. It stays available to view and to share for as long as the item exists, and it transfers to the next owner rather than starting again.

    What makes us different

    A paper certificate is only as good
    as the company that printed it

    Letters get forged. Registers get lost when a business is sold or closes. Databases get edited by whoever owns them. Anchoring the certificate to a public blockchain removes all three problems at once, and it is the reason a VeriChain number still answers long after the paper has yellowed.

    The established model

    • ×A printed letter, which can be copied or altered
    • ×A private register only the issuer can read or change
    • ×Verification depends on the company still trading
    • ×Provenance restarts each time the item is sold
    • ×Nothing proves when the opinion was actually given

    VeriChain

    • ✓The certificate is hashed and anchored to a public chain
    • ✓Anyone can read the entry — no account, no fee
    • ✓The record outlives us. It does not depend on our servers
    • ✓Ownership transfers extend the history rather than reset it
    • ✓The issue date is timestamped and cannot be backdated

    The examination has not changed — it is still a person with the item in hand, comparing it against exemplars. What has changed is what happens to that opinion once it is given, and how long it stays checkable. For the life of the item, at no further cost.

    Other authentication results

    When an item does not receive a Letter

    Not every examination ends in a Letter of Authenticity. Where it does not, we still write down what we found and why, so you are left with a documented opinion rather than a refusal.

    LOO

    Letter of Opinion

    A rejection opinion, explaining why we consider the autograph questionable or inconsistent with authentic examples of that signer. Issued when an item fails authentication, so you have our reasoning in writing rather than a bare no.

    CH

    Clubhouse Letter

    Identifies memorabilia that was ghost-signed without any intent to deceive — signed by a batboy, a staff member, a secretary or a family member rather than by the named athlete or celebrity. The item is genuine of its kind; the hand is simply not the one on the label.

    INC

    Inconclusive Letter

    Issued where our authenticators cannot reach a reliable conclusion either way. In these cases we provide a credit voucher for the full fee, to be used against a future submission.

    Fees still apply. They cover the examination itself rather than the outcome, so a Letter of Opinion or a Clubhouse Letter is chargeable in the same way as a Letter of Authenticity. An inconclusive result is the exception: the fee comes back to you as credit.

    Additional services

    House calls

    Confidential authentication at your home, office, warehouse or shop, for collections large enough that posting them is not sensible. An authenticator travels to you, examines the items in front of you and completes the work on the spot.

    Because an authenticator travels, a house call carries a higher service fee than the standard options. Travel and accommodation are quoted separately where they apply.

    Witnessed on site

    Signed in front of us

    Bring an unsigned item to an event where a signing is taking place and our authenticator watches the pen touch the item. Nothing is left to opinion, so there is no examination to fail and the certificate is issued on the spot.

    Items already signed elsewhere are examined the usual way, on site, while you wait.

    How an item is examined

    How it works

    You are never charged
    before we see the item

    We take no payment details at submission. Our desk prices the item once it is in hand, and we invoice you only after you have agreed the figure.

      At the desk

      What the examination covers

      01

      The signature itself

      Slant, flow, pen pressure, letter size and rhythm, compared against exemplars held in our reference library for that signer and that period.

      02

      Ink, surface and age

      How the ink sits on the surface, how it has aged, and whether either is consistent with the date the item is said to come from.

      03

      The record

      A certification number is issued and written into a public record that cannot be edited afterwards. Anyone can look it up without an account.

      04

      Anchored to the blockchain

      The signed-off certificate is hashed and that fingerprint is written to a public chain. The signer, the photograph, the notes and the date are fixed at that moment, and any later alteration fails verification.

      Step four

      Anchored to the ledger

      When the desk signs off, the certificate is generated, the verification page is published, the QR code is produced and the ledger entry is written — in a single action. The signer, the item images, the examination notes and the date are fixed at that moment.

      Any later change to any of it produces a different fingerprint and fails verification immediately. That is what makes the record tamper-evident rather than merely stored.

      Because the proof is digital, it exists before the item is back in your hands. You can send a buyer the verification link while the parcel is still with the courier.

      Worth being clear about

      What the ledger does, and what it does not

      The ledger guarantees that this certificate is the one we issued and that nothing in it has changed since. It fixes the record, the date and the images beyond reach.

      It does not, by itself, make a signature authentic. That is a judgement made by an authenticator with the item in hand, under light and magnification. The ledger secures our opinion. It does not replace it, and we would not want it to.

      Fees

      You agree the figure first

      No payment details are taken at submission. Once the item is at our desk we confirm the certification type and the fee. If either has changed we tell you the new figure and wait for your agreement before any invoice is raised.

      Outcomes

      If an item does not pass

      We return it with a written result and no certificate. Fees cover the examination itself, so they apply whatever the outcome — we tell you that before you pay rather than afterwards.

      Where an item carries several signatures, each is examined and priced separately. If some pass and others do not, the certificate names only those that passed.

      A failed result is anchored to the chain in the same way as a pass. The record states what we found, and it cannot be quietly removed later.

      About

      Independent, and paid to be right

      VeriChain Authentication exists to answer one question about a signed item: is it real. We render an opinion, record it permanently, and have no interest in what the item then sells for.

      We do not buy, sell or broker

      An authenticator who also deals has a reason to prefer one answer over another. We do neither, which is the whole point of asking a third party in the first place. Our opinion is the product, and it is worth exactly as much as our willingness to give an unwelcome one.

      Every examination happens in the hand, under light and magnification, against exemplars we hold for that signer and that period. We do not render opinions from photographs.

      Results are written into a record that cannot be edited once issued. When an item changes hands, the certificate travels with it, so its history gets longer rather than starting again.
